why:
entities are DECLARED by a component (RFC-0043/0044); see the node stage's `rust:Node`.

phase-483 W3 — re-keyed from `DeclaredNode`: the declarative constructors are now the `nros::DeclarativeNode` extension trait on `nros::Node`, so a component's node and a program's node are one type.

Issue 2038 (2026-10-25, resolved): a declared timer has issue 1974's two facilities now.
  * CALL INFO: every declared timer's callback reads `CallbackCtx::timer_info()` (`Some(&TimerCallInfo)` in a timer callback, `None` elsewhere).
  * AUTOSTART: `create_timer_for_callback_name_with_autostart(name, period, clock, autostart)`. `false` registers the timer cancelled; `EntityMetadata::timer_autostart` carries the flag to the runtime.

There is ONE registrar: `node_runtime` registers every declared timer through `Executor::register_timer_with_info`, the call `rust:Node::create_timer_with_info` makes. Its arena entry is the one `register_timer_on_clock` built, so an armed timer behaves as before.

NOT YET: a component cannot START a timer it declared stopped. No declarative handle reaches `Executor::reset_timer`; see issue 2038's Still open.
